description: Figure 19 is a grouped bar chart illustrating the average probing accuracy difference for two multilingual BERT models, mBERT (light blue bars) and XLM-R (dark blue bars), across four different MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) variations. The horizontal axis lists the MLP configurations, which are labeled as "hidden:[size], activation_function", with the size indicated in square brackets (e.g., [50], [100], [50, 50]) and the activation function specified as either "linear" or "ReLU". The vertical axis is labeled "% point difference" and uses a linear scale ranging from -0.2 to +0.2, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Each configuration has two adjacent bars, one for each model. For the "hidden:[50], linear" configuration, the mBERT bar extends down to approximately -0.05, while the XLM-R bar extends up to approximately +0.15. For the "hidden:[], linear" configuration, the mBERT bar extends up to approximately +0.08, and the XLM-R bar extends up to approximately +0.20. For the "hidden:[100], ReLU" configuration, the mBERT bar extends down to approximately -0.08, and the XLM-R bar extends up to approximately +0.03. For the "hidden:[50, 50], ReLU" configuration, the mBERT bar extends down to approximately -0.15, and the XLM-R bar extends down to approximately -0.10. The bars are not sorted; they are presented in the order listed on the x-axis. There are no visual elements like shading, bolding, or annotations to emphasize any particular bar.
